newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends little changed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends little changed.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended little changed in another listless trading with a firmer Tokyo market helping RSS grades of rubber, dealers said.
SMR grades of rubber hovered at around overnight levels as demand remained lacking, they said. "We don't see much demand interest from users," a dealer at a trading firm said.
Only scattered interest from Taiwan and South Korea was seen for nearby SMR grades.
Demand from Europe was also sluggish because many buyers were still adjusting themselves after the summer holiday.
Domestic rubber production was thin not only in Malaysia but also in Thailand and Indonesia which kept some producers from selling at current levels.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set indicator price for Oct RSS1 buyer at 328.50 cents ($1.31) a kg, up half a cent. Oct SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 313.50 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 250.87 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 11 from 251.48 on Sept 10. The daily indicator price was 249.99 against 250.20.
